title: feat(pm): add the stale `finding` label sweep (D1)
body:
Part of #16904 — deliverable **D1 only**. The card stays open for D2 (the report-only patrol row in `check-half-states.mjs`), so this body carries no closing keyword.

## What and why

The PM state model defines `finding` as transient — 「定级即离标」 — but nothing mechanises the strip, so a graded card keeps the marker and `label:finding` stops answering the one question it exists for. Three independent measurements on this card: 385 of 395 open carriers already graded, then 185 of 226 two days later, then 38 of 100 stripped by hand on objectstack.

This adds the one-time sweep, `scripts/pm/sweep-stale-finding.mjs`: **dry run by default**, `--repo owner/name` for either board, `--write` to act, bounded batches with a `GET /rate_limit` reading printed before and after each, a stop on the first `403`/`429` that prints `--cursor=N` to resume, and `--self-test` offline with no token. Each removal is the four-step write — read the card's labels, compute the survivor set, write, read back and diff — and **any** difference refuses to proceed rather than racing another actor.

It only ever subtracts one label: it adds nothing, synthesises no grade, posts no comment and touches no assignee. A card carrying `finding` with **no** grade is the genuinely ungraded pool and is left alone; a `pm:seat` post is never touched. Both are reported rather than silently skipped. ⛔ The script is **not run against either board by this PR** — the seat that owns a board runs it once, by hand, after reading a dry run.

### One measured deviation from the ruled shape

The grading fixed step 3 as "write the full set". `scripts/check-whole-set-label-write.mjs` **bans** the whole-set replace across `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**` and `scripts/**` — its header carries the measurement, a label destroyed one second after it was written by another writer's whole-set replace. So step 3 is `DELETE .../labels/finding`, the one verb that names a single label and cannot rewrite a set. The four steps and the computed survivor set are unchanged (the survivor set is what step 4 diffs against); only the verb that realises it changed, and it strictly improves the property the read-back exists to detect. That gate is in this PR's derived set and passes.

The file surface stays at **one new file**: `check-self-test-wired` and `check-self-test-workflow-commands` both pass with no `package.json` entry, because their population is scripts a workflow names. ⚠️ The consequence, stated rather than left implicit: **no workflow runs this self-test**, so the instrument is unfired in CI until someone wires it — a one-line follow-up for the seat, alongside D2.

## Acceptance

| reading | result |
|:--|:--|
| `node scripts/pm/sweep-stale-finding.mjs --self-test` | **exit 0** — 91 cases across 9 batteries, offline, no token |
| required case: `finding` + `pm:queue` is stale | pass, and the row names the trigger |
| required case: `finding` + `priority:p3` is stale (no state at all) | pass |
| required case: `finding` alone is **not** stale | pass — reported as the ungraded pool, not skipped |
| required case: a `pm:seat` post is never touched | pass, whatever else it carries |
| required case: the four-step write refuses when the read-back differs | pass — driven offline, a fixture re-adds a label after the write; the run stops on the first card and the second is never written to |
| required case: the `403`/`429` stop prints the cursor | pass — a 403 fixture on card 2 stops the run, prints `--cursor=22`, exit 4, and card 3 is never touched |
| required case: `--dry-run` writes nothing (write-path spy) | pass — every request the dry run issued is a `GET`, and not one of them is a per-card label read |
| ablation A: the ungraded verdict flipped to stale | **7 of 91 cases red**; restored to the byte-identical HEAD blob (`5167082…`), green again |
| ablation B: the dry-run mode gate deleted from the batch builder | **5 of 91 cases red**, write-path spy among them; restored, green again |
| live `--dry-run` against `objectstack-ai/objectstack` (exit captured before any pipe) | **exit 0** — listed **42** open cards carrying `finding`; **19 stale**, **23** genuinely ungraded, **0** unjudged; `rate_limit` printed at run-start and run-end (core 14871/15000) |
| stale by trigger on that run | 13 `pm:blocked` · 3 `pm:on-hold` · 2 priority-only · 1 `pm:dispatched` |
| control — a label that cannot be stale | `pm:seat`: **13** open, **0** stale under the same exported predicate. Positive leg, so the zero is a measurement and not a silence: the same harness reads **19** stale over the `finding` population, matching the tool's own run |
| derived gates (`dispatch-gates --commands`, reconciled with `--ran`) | **29 derived, 29 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**, every one `exit 0` — including `check-whole-set-label-write`, `check-self-test-wired`, `check-self-test-workflow-commands`, `check-scripts-symbol-anchors`, `check-nul-bytes` |
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide, `eslint . --no-inline-config`) | **exit 0** at `b9f45331`, 1m12s — no narrowing claimed |

Changeset: `skip-changeset`. `scripts/pm/**` ships in no package's `files[]`, so nothing published moves.

## Acceptance notes

- The stale predicate is a **disjunction** (a grading state **or** a priority), as ruled. The triage seat's "state **and** priority" constraint was learned from filling a *missing* priority by hand and sweeping a decision card into the queue; it binds a sweep that writes a grade. This one only subtracts, so it cannot make that error, and under subtraction the conjunction would leave standing exactly the cards the index is wrongest about. Every stale row names its trigger, so the set stays auditable card by card.
- The live reading shows the population has moved since the card's last measurement (62 stale on 09-12 → 19 stale of 42 carriers today), and that 16 of the 19 sit beside `pm:blocked` / `pm:on-hold` — the exact set the last hand pass deliberately left for "a lower-risk pass". The by-trigger breakdown in the report is what makes that visible before anyone writes.
- noted, not filed: the sweep is rung 3 of the fix. While a grading write can leave the label behind, the population refills; the write-path half is already tracked separately.
